operations.name: new_part
operations.summary: Creates a new part document from a template (or SolidWorks' configured default part template) and returns its identity. Always the first step of a build from scratch: call this before any other document-scoped operation, then pass the returned 'title' as documentName in every subsequent step.

params.name: templatePath
params.description: Absolute path to a .prtdot template. Omit to use SolidWorks' configured default part template (swDefaultTemplatePart).

operations.name: select_by_id
operations.summary: Selects (or adds to selection) one entity by name and type, populating the SolidWorks selection list that subsequent operations (extrude, fillet, pattern, ...) consume. Common type values: PLANE, FACE, VERTEX, SKETCH, BODYFEATURE, AXIS, SKETCHSEGMENT, DATUMPOINT. mark distinguishes the role of a selection for a multi-selection feature (e.g. extrude_boss just needs mark 0 on the sketch/profile). WARNING for EDGE: the x/y/z hint point behaves like a view-dependent screen pick, not a reliable model-space identity — UAT proved it silently selects a DIFFERENT edge than intended after the part's topology changes (e.g. a cut added since the coordinates were chosen), and it silently refuses to select some back-facing edges entirely, both while still reporting selectionCount as if nothing were wrong. Prefer select_by_ray for EDGE and FACE selection — it is view-independent and did not miss once across the same test.

params.name: name
params.description: Entity name, e.g. 'Front Plane', 'Sketch1', 'Boss-Extrude1'.

params.name: type
params.description: SolidWorks selection type string, e.g. 'PLANE', 'SKETCH', 'FACE', 'EDGE', 'AXIS', 'BODYFEATURE'.

params.name: x
params.description: Hint point X, used to disambiguate overlapping entities; 0 is fine when the name is unique.

params.name: append
params.description: true to add to the current selection instead of replacing it.

params.name: mark
params.description: Selection mark/role — see the recipe that consumes this selection for the mark it expects.

params.name: callout
params.description: Always a null COM callout reference; not settable.

operations.name: insert_sketch
operations.summary: Starts editing a new 2D sketch on the currently selected plane or face. Select a plane first (select_by_id, type PLANE) then call this. SolidWorks' InsertSketch toggles sketch-edit mode — the same COM member also exits a sketch; see 'exit_sketch'.

operations.name: exit_sketch
operations.summary: Exits the currently active sketch, returning to the feature tree. SolidWorks' InsertSketch toggles sketch-edit mode, so this calls the same COM member as 'insert_sketch' — the difference is only the precondition and the expected resulting state.
operations.verifiedOn: SolidWorks 2026 SP3.0, live (tests/SeedVerifier/Zoo.Live.cs sk.InsertSketch(true) called a second time to exit)

operations.name: create_circle_by_radius
operations.summary: Adds a circle to the active sketch, centered at (centerX, centerY) in sketch space (centerZ is always 0 on a planar sketch). Requires an active sketch — call insert_sketch first. Use two calls with different radii, same center, to sketch a washer profile.

params.name: centerX
params.description: Sketch-space X of the circle center.

params.name: centerY
params.description: Sketch-space Y of the circle center.

Select the sketch first (select_by_id, type SKETCH, mark 0), make sure no sketch is being edited (exit_sketch), then call this. Leave every param but depth1 at its default for a simple one-direction boss.

operations.name: undo
operations.summary: Undoes the last N document edits. No operation ever triggers this automatically (ADR 0002: fail-fast, no auto-rollback) — call it deliberately to back out of a partial state after a failed step. IModelDoc2.EditUndo2 is void — SolidWorks gives no status code for this call, so its own success cannot be verified by return value (a documented limitation, not an oversight: the 'noNewRebuildErrors' check below confirms the document is still in a clean, rebuildable state afterward, which is the closest real post-condition the API offers). Compare 'documentState.featureCount'/'selectionCount' across the surrounding steps in the transcript to confirm what actually changed.

params.name: steps
params.description: Number of edits to undo.

operations.verifiedOn: Signature-verified against SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks (IModelDoc2.EditUndo2(Int32) -> Void); not exercised by the live zoo build. See ADR 0002's open question on EditUndo3 reliability for compound API-driven state — EditUndo2 is used here as the simpler, documented member.

operations.name: cut_extrude
operations.summary: Cut-extrudes the pre-selected sketch profile, removing material. Select the sketch first (select_by_id, type SKETCH, mark 0), exit sketch mode, then call. Mirrors extrude_boss's params but calls FeatureCut4 (27 params — a different, longer signature than extrude_boss's FeatureExtrusion3). If this fails verification (returnNotNull/featureCountIncreased), the single most common cause is the cut extruding AWAY from the material instead of into it (docs/seed-verification.md §4.7) — retry with reverseDirection true before assuming anything else is wrong.

params.description: Sd — cut in one direction only.

params.name: flipSideToCut
params.description: Flip — cut the other side of the sketch profile.

params.name: reverseDirection
params.description: Dir — reverse the cut direction; try true first if the cut returns nothing.

params.name: endCondition1
params.description: T1. 0 = Blind (uses depth1), 1 = Through-All.

params.name: endCondition2
params.description: T2, direction 2 (only used when not singleDirection).

params.name: depth1
params.description: D1 — blind depth, direction 1. Required in practice for endCondition1=Blind.

params.name: depth2
params.description: D2 — blind depth, direction 2.

params.name: normalCut
params.description: Cut normal to the sketch surface rather than along the sketch plane's own normal.

params.name: startCondition
params.description: T0. 0 = swStartSketchPlane.

operations.name: fillet_constant_radius

params.name: radius
params.description: R1 — the constant fillet radius.

params.name: radius2

params.name: rho
params.description: Rho — conic parameter for a conic (P-curve) fillet; ignored for filletType=0.

params.name: filletType
params.description: Ftyp. 0 = simple/constant radius.

params.name: conicTypeForCurvature
params.description: ConicRhoType.

params.name: radiiArray
params.description: Radii — per-edge radii for a multi-radius fillet; comNull for a simple fillet.

params.name: distance2Array
params.description: Dist2Arr — second distances, for a distance-distance fillet; comNull for a simple fillet.

params.name: rhoArray

params.name: setbackDistances
params.description: SetBackDistances — for a setback vertex fillet; comNull for a simple fillet.

operations.name: select_by_ray
operations.summary: Selects the entity hit by a model-space ray (IModelDocExtension.SelectByRay) — view-independent, unlike select_by_id's coordinate hint, and the reliable way to pick an edge or face. Point (x,y,z) is the ray origin, (rx,ry,rz) the direction (a plain direction vector, not a unit-carrying length — component magnitudes only need to be consistent with each other, not any particular unit), radius the pick tolerance. type is a swSelectType_e integer (1=EDGE, 2=FACE, 3=VERTEX). AIMING, empirically verified across two UAT passes: the pick is NOT a fixed-radius model-space tolerance despite how 'radius' reads — it behaves like a cone that widens with range from the ray origin to the target, so the SAME radius that picks correctly from close range can pick a neighboring edge/face from farther away (confirmed: origin 10mm from the target picked correctly every time; origin 30mm away picked a completely different, unrelated edge, same radius, same direction). Aim SIDE-ON at the MID-LENGTH of the target edge, from CLOSE range (a few mm to a couple cm), not from far away. Never aim collinearly DOWN an edge's own length — a ray traveling parallel to the edge terminates at whichever vertex it reaches first, and most edges share that vertex with two or three others, which is the ambiguity that produces a wrong pick. There is no error or warning when a ray picks the 'wrong but real' neighboring entity instead of missing outright — success is reported either way — so a slightly-off aim is a genuinely silent failure mode; check documentState.selectedEntities (every run_operation/run_operations response includes it once something is selected) to confirm the descriptor (edge length, midpoint) matches what you intended before trusting the result.

params.name: x
params.description: Ray origin X. Keep this close to the target entity (a few mm to a couple cm) — aiming from far away lets the pick cone drift onto a neighboring edge/face even with a small radius.

params.name: y
params.description: Ray origin Y.

params.name: z
params.description: Ray origin Z.

params.name: rx
params.description: Ray direction X component (unitless). Aim side-on at the target edge/face's mid-length, not collinear along its own length — a collinear ray terminates at a shared vertex, which is ambiguous between the edges meeting there.

params.name: ry
params.description: Ray direction Y component (unitless).

params.name: rz
params.description: Ray direction Z component (unitless); default points -Z, i.e. straight down onto a part sketched on Front/Top. For a vertical edge, a ray straight down whose origin sits directly above that edge's column is exactly the side-on-at-mid-length aim this recipe needs.

params.name: radius
params.description: Pick tolerance around the ray — but see the summary: its effective width scales with range from the origin to the target, so this alone does not make a long-range aim reliable.

params.name: type
params.description: 1 = EDGE, 2 = FACE, 3 = VERTEX.

params.name: append
params.description: true to add to the current selection instead of replacing it.

operations.verifiedOn: Promoted from docs/uat-registered-operations.json — UAT-verified live across two passes: picked the correct 6 mm vertical edge at both the front and back corner of a plate where select_by_id picked the wrong edge or refused entirely (docs/uat-ladder-report.md B3/rung2f), and, on re-verdict, a 5-aim x 2-topology matrix confirmed the topology-change failure mode is fully gone but surfaced the distance-dependent aiming behavior documented above (docs/uat-ladder-report.md RE-VERDICT gap #2: same radius, same direction, origin at 10mm picked correctly every time, origin at 30mm picked a 40mm neighbor edge every time). Signature matches IModelDocExtension.SelectByRay(11 params) confirmed independently against SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.

operations.name: set_material
operations.summary: Applies a SolidWorks material to the part (IPartDoc.SetMaterialPropertyName2). database is usually 'SOLIDWORKS Materials' or the full path to a .sldmat file; name is the material name as shown in the material tree, e.g. '6061 Alloy'. configuration '' means the active configuration. This call is void — SolidWorks gives no status code, so it cannot be verified by return value here; get_part_info's mass figure is the practical readback (an unassigned part computes mass at 1000 kg/m^3, so a mass matching the expected material's density is the confirmation this worked).

params.name: configuration
params.description: Configuration name; '' means the active configuration.

params.name: database
params.description: Material database name or full path to a .sldmat file.

params.name: name
params.description: Material name as shown in the material tree, e.g. '6061 Alloy'.

operations.verifiedOn: Promoted from docs/uat-registered-operations.json — UAT-verified live: '6061 Alloy' from 'SOLIDWORKS Materials' produced an implied density of exactly 2700 kg/m^3 in get_part_info's mass figure (docs/uat-ladder-report.md rung 3).
